note: Single source of truth for completion standards. The method document explains criteria and reasoning only and must not restate these numbers — a duplicated copy always drifts. scripts/check-report.mjs reads this file. Shape-specific steps fire from an explicit manifest.shape, never guessed from the report text.
reportOutlineNote: The sections a finished report contains, in order. The steps below say what evidence to gather; this says what the reader receives. Headings are given in English because the method is English-only; render them in the language the report is written in. Without this list every run invents its own outline — measured across six runs on one product, reports came back with 11 to 17 sections under different names, and required sections such as customer voice and relative scale appeared in some and vanished from others. An agent may write these in one pass or one at a time; that is a runtime decision, and having the list is what makes writing them one at a time possible.

reportOutline.heading: Read this first
reportOutline.must: What it is, who pays, what it costs, where it sits, the biggest opportunity and the biggest risk — in one paragraph a busy reader can stop after.

reportOutline.heading: Primary viewpoint
reportOutline.must: Whose decision this report serves (buyer / founder / investor / PM) and what changes because of that choice.

reportOutline.heading: Category definition
reportOutline.must: Who pays; what work it does and on what object; input to output; where the workflow ends; how it is delivered.

reportOutline.heading: Site inventory
reportOutline.must: What the site's own index says: how many pages, in how many languages, of what kinds. Which standard paths exist, which returned 404, which were blocked. Counted, never estimated.

reportOutline.heading: Capabilities
reportOutline.must: Each capability: what it manages, what it does to it, which plan it is in. Prose, not a bare table.

reportOutline.heading: Core user journey
reportOutline.must: Signup to first value, step by step, and where the friction is.

reportOutline.heading: Pricing teardown
reportOutline.must: Every tier with its unit, what changes between tiers, and what is not published. An enterprise-sales product still needs this section — say how it is sold.

reportOutline.heading: Claims versus facts
reportOutline.must: A table: each vendor claim, the evidence found, and a verdict. Verdicts other than 'unverifiable' require arithmetic or a source.

reportOutline.heading: Company fundamentals
reportOutline.must: Founded, HQ, founders, funding, headcount, revenue, valuation — each with its source or marked missing. Name the operating company when it differs from the product.

reportOutline.heading: Competitive landscape
reportOutline.must: Layered by what each player does, not by fame. Only products whose own site was opened may be called direct competitors; everything else is labelled unverified.

reportOutline.heading: Scale and relative position
reportOutline.must: Domain rank and its 30-day direction for the product and its named peers, with the caveat that a rank is prominence and not traffic. Plus at least two other proxies.

reportOutline.heading: Voice of the customer
reportOutline.must: Verbatim customer wording with source and date, positive and negative and suggestions, and the sampling rule. If every channel refused, say which and what was tried.

reportOutline.heading: Recent developments
reportOutline.must: The last 30 days, dated: releases, pricing changes, funding, incidents. If the newest item is months old, say so rather than presenting it as recent.

reportOutline.heading: Risks
reportOutline.must: What would have to be true for this to go wrong, ordered by how much it would cost the reader.

reportOutline.heading: Conclusions and recommendations
reportOutline.must: Answers written for the viewpoint declared at the top. For a buyer: who should and should not choose this, and what to verify before signing.

reportOutline.heading: Boundaries of this report
reportOutline.must: What was not obtained, which channels were tried, and how each gap limits the conclusions.

reportOutline.heading: Appendix: evidence list
reportOutline.must: Every source cited in the body, with its id and URL.

reportOutlineConditional.heading: Licence and the open-source boundary
reportOutlineConditional.must: Which licence, what it covers, what the paid edition adds, and what self-hosting actually costs.

reportOutlineConditional.heading: Supply side
reportOutlineConditional.must: Listing velocity from the new-arrivals feed and the category structure. Never count sellers from the sitemap.

reportOutlineConditional.heading: Demand side
reportOutlineConditional.must: Where buyers come from and what they search for, measured rather than assumed.

failureReasons.blocked: Every fallback channel was tried and failed. State which ones and what each returned.
failureReasons.absent: The thing does not exist (no mobile app means no app store reviews).
failureReasons.incapable: The environment genuinely cannot do it. You must have actually tried, and must quote the command and the error.

steps.name: Viewpoint
steps.requires: State the primary viewpoint up front (buyer / founder / investor / PM)

check.pattern: 主要读者|主视角|视角|[Pp]rimary reader|[Vv]iewpoint|[Ww]ritten for|[Pp]erspective

steps.name: Path space
steps.requires: Results from sitemap / llms.txt / robots.txt — before any path probing

steps.name: Site inventory
steps.requires: apex + www + ≥12 paths + ≥5 subdomains, with 200 / 404 / blocked kept separate

steps.name: Supply side (marketplace only)
steps.requires: Listing velocity from the new-arrivals feed, plus category structure. Do not count sellers from the sitemap
steps.why: Field test: zero sellers in the sitemap, but the RSS declared in robots.txt yields ~455 new listings/day (C-39)

steps.name: Index pages opened
steps.requires: The body text of every pricing / quota / limit / rate-limit / error-code page in the index

steps.name: First-party evidence
steps.requires: ≥3 verbatim quotes from first-party pages. The pricing page must be confirmed after rendering, with every interactive control operated

steps.name: License teardown (open source only)
steps.requires: Read the full LICENSE to locate the paywalled directories; check its commit history for the direction of change
steps.why: The exact paywall coordinates appear only in LICENSE; and license changes hide inside ordinary refactor commits (C-32, C-34)

steps.name: Screenshots
steps.requires: ≥3 images saved to disk and embedded in the report, each with the judgement it supports
steps.fallback: A login wall is not a reason — pull frames from the vendor's own video channel (see casebook C-05)

steps.name: Customer case studies
steps.requires: If a case study page exists, read ≥3 including the most recent one, and record each one's year
steps.skipWhen: site has no case study page

steps.name: Claims list
steps.requires: ≥5 homepage claims, each marked holds / fails / unverifiable with its evidence

steps.name: Company fundamentals
steps.requires: Seven fields with a value or an explicit "searched, not found"; ≥2 independent corroborating signals; headcount must carry a date

steps.name: Landscape scan
steps.requires: Pricing page text from ≥3 competitors' own sites, normalised to one billing unit

steps.name: Layering
steps.requires: Layer before comparing: are these players doing the same job? Every layer needs an anchor inside the reliable range

steps.name: Scale and structure
steps.requires: Domain rank plus 30-day trend for every player; ≥2 proxy dimensions; state the measure and its distortion

check.pattern: Tranco|口径说明|domain rank|prominence rank|what (this|the) (measure|rank) means

steps.name: Demand side (marketplace only)
steps.requires: State explicitly whether the demand side is measurable. Never pass total site traffic off as buyer volume

check.pattern: 需求侧|买家规模|无法验证|不可测|demand side|buyer (volume|scale)|could not be verified|unmeasurable

steps.why: Field test: total site rank mixes buyers, sellers and storefront-link traffic; it cannot be split (C-42)

steps.name: Voice of customer
steps.requires: ≥1 third-party review source with concrete content; verbatim quotes with source and date; positive / negative / suggestions all present; state the sampling rule

steps.name: Recent changes
steps.requires: Last 30 days: releases, pricing changes, funding, incidents, user reaction — each dated

check.pattern: 近 ?30 ?天|近期变化|近期动态|最近.{0,4}(个月|周)|20\d\d-\d\d-\d\d|20\d\d ?年 ?\d{1,2} ?月|[Ll]ast 30 days|[Rr]ecent changes

steps.name: Official video channel
steps.requires: Skim the vendor's video channel title list; treat it as a changelog
steps.why: Field test, twice: a core integration absent from the site and the docs appeared only in an official video

steps.name: Opening summary
steps.requires: A jargon-free summary: what it is, who buys it, how much it earns, where it sits, the opportunity and the risk

check.pattern: 先读这段|一句话结论|摘要|[Rr]ead this first|TL;?DR|[Ss]ummary

steps.name: Boundaries
steps.requires: What was not obtained, and how that limits the conclusions. Not "what I didn't do"

check.pattern: 本报告的边界|未取得|信息边界|[Bb]oundaries|[Nn]ot obtained|[Ww]hat (we|I) could ?n.t get
